notes.H07: The passage describes grief at the loss of a dear friend: everything darkened, every place hated for lacking him, eyes searching everywhere. That speaks to losing your dog, whom you call your closest friend and your reason to come home each day. The passage names the grief rather than offering a way through it.
notes.H14: The passage is about keeping faith with a friend, and says that revealing his secrets destroys the friendship. That speaks to one side of your dilemma, the worry about betraying your friend. It says nothing about the wife or what might be owed to her, so it covers only half of what you describe.
notes.H21: The passage says a close friend, someone trusted who shared bread, has turned against the speaker. That speaks to your best friend telling your boyfriend after you confided in her. It doesn't say why such a betrayal happens, so it doesn't answer your question about why she did it.
notes.AS21: Gibran lists the clothes, meals and beds that come from other people's hands, and asks how anyone can separate from others. That speaks to the sense of owing your family a great deal. It is a statement about how bound people are to each other. It does not address becoming independent or guilt.
notes.AS39: The passage says money wrings tears and toil from people, and that owning wealth brings its own worry. It speaks to the tears over money you describe. Its subject is greed and the anxieties of those who hold riches, not debt that grows despite careful living, so it fits only part of what you wrote.
